verdictReason: Killed, moderate confidence: the only edge is price ($495 vs $1,500), which is not an edge. An attorney incumbent offers a free review and free advice (covers the $99 review tier), sells 'human attorney review only' with about 610 reviews, calls non-law-firm plans 'unprivileged' and says not to pay non-lawyers for IP; other law-firm blogs say a lawyer is not required. Trust gap for a no-record entrant; assumption-based pessimistic year-1 profit about -$6.3k. Not verified: UPL exposure, cheap-consultant tier, free template.

answers.question: (1) What free/cheap alternative covers the wedge?
answers.answer: The $99 review tier is covered free: AMZ Sellers Attorney says its review is free and starts the same business day and its service pages offer a free evaluation and 'free advice' (a funnel to the paid appeal). DIY is explicitly viable: one law-firm blog says a lawyer is not required, and another law firm's blog calls the plan 'an exercise in persuasive writing' and lists writing it yourself or hiring an online consultant as routes. A free reusable plan-of-action template exists (amzbase, scan-1 evidence SVC-03-E4/E5, not re-fetched: the page was refused). The $495 tier is a cheaper substitute for $1,500 attorney flat fees, so the buyer's alternative set is free template + free attorney review at the bottom, $1,500 attorneys at the top.

answers.question: (2) What structural edge exists and who could copy it?
answers.answer: None. A single-category scope, flat fee and AI-assisted drafting are not edges: any consultant or attorney firm can quote a narrower scope, and the incumbents already concede that metric cases are often within reach of a competent plan-of-action service. The only potentially compounding asset is a private archive of accepted plans by notice type, which needs many paid cases first, and a no-case-history stranger has none. Trust is the scarce input and incumbents hold it (about 610 reviews, attorney privilege framing, 'human attorney review only'). Falsifier: 30+ real simple-category cases at $495 with a reinstatement rate at or above attorney claims and refund rate under 15% would show a durable cheap-tier niche; nothing public shows this.

answers.question: (3) Who demonstrably pays and how much?
answers.answer: Sellers with frozen accounts pay attorney firms flat fees of $1,500 (most appeals) and $2,300 (IP and related), and the leading firm cites about 610 third-party reviews (self-reported); The Appeal Guru $1,495 per appeal with repeat appeals free (scan-1 evidence SVC-03-E2, not re-fetched) and Amazon Global Appeals about 495 GBP (SVC-03-E3, unclear, old). I found no public evidence of buyers paying $495 to an unknown non-lawyer; the paying segment is buying credibility and legal framing the entrant lacks.

answers.question: (4) Legal/platform constraints?
answers.answer: Unauthorised practice of law was not verifiable: primary sources (Nolo, Wikipedia) were refused by the fetch tool and the search budget ran out, so exposure by state is unknown. Verified signals: an Amazon-seller attorney tells sellers not to pay anyone who is not an admitted lawyer for intellectual property issues (so the entrant must exclude IP, safety and anything legal-sounding), and incumbents market that a non-law-firm plan of action is an unprivileged document. Amazon decides appeals through Seller Performance and rules change; no Amazon terms about third-party preparers were read. The owner would have to submit the plan from their own account; the entrant should never take credentials. Unrecoverable cases (fraud, forged documents, repeated violations) per scan-1 evidence SVC-03-E6 not re-fetched.

answers.question: (5) Year-1 numbers (reference entrant: $650 start, 12 h/week)?
answers.answer: Base: 22 cases (assumption: about 2/month from month 2) x 70% net of refunds x $495 plus 16 reviews x $99 = $9,207 revenue; costs $6,683 (startup $650, tools $360, ads $4,800 at an assumed $400/month, one-time legal review of terms and disclaimers $500, payment fees $373) = about $2.5k profit before roughly 600 owner hours. Pessimistic (price x0.8, volume x0.5, cost x1.5): revenue $3,683, cost $10,025, profit about -$6,342. All volumes, refund rates and ad costs are assumptions; no public source gives conversion or CPC for this niche.

killReasons.reason: The $99 review tier is covered free: an attorney incumbent gives a free review that starts the same business day and free advice, using it as a funnel; the DIY route is endorsed by law-firm blogs and a free template exists.

The $495 tier has no edge beyond price: incumbents already market 'human attorney review only', a non-law-firm plan as an 'unprivileged document', and about 610 reviews, while the entrant has no reviews, no case history and no attorney; buyers with frozen funds pay for credibility. A discount is not an edge.

Legal exposure: an attorney source says not to pay non-lawyers for IP matters and UPL by state was not researched; this limits the entrant to the narrowest categories where the incumbent concedes plans are cheap to produce.
Pessimistic year-1 model (price x0.8, volume x0.5, cost x1.5) is negative (about -$6.3k), and base profit is about $2.5k for roughly 600 owner hours; inputs are assumptions.
Some suspensions are unrecoverable (repeated violations, fraud, forged documents), so a low price risks adverse selection into refund-heavy cases (scan-1 evidence, not re-fetched).

assumptions: Prices $495 per appeal and $99 per Plan of Action review (given in the case file).
Cases: 22 in year 1 (about 2/month from month 2) and 16 reviews (about 1.5/month); assumption, no public conversion or lead data.
30% of appeal cases are refunded or unrecoverable (assumption; no public simple-category success rate for a new entrant). Reviews are non-refundable.

Costs: startup $650 (reference entrant), tools/hosting $360, paid ads $400/month = $4,800 (assumption; CPC for suspension keywords unverified and likely contested by attorney firms), one-time lawyer review of terms and disclaimers $500 (assumption), payment fees 2.9% + $0.30 = $373 (assumption on standard card rates); total $6,683, excludes owner labour (about 600 h).
Pessimistic: price x0.8 ($396 / $79), volume x0.5 (11 cases, 8 reviews), revenue $3,683; base cost x1.5 = $10,025; profit about -$6,342.

legalNotes: Unauthorised practice of law (UPL) was not verifiable: Nolo and Wikipedia pages were refused by the fetch tool and the web-search budget was exhausted; exposure varies by state and is unknown.

An Amazon-seller law firm states 'you should not pay anybody who is not an admitted lawyer' for intellectual property issues (D7); incumbents also describe a non-law-firm plan of action as an unprivileged document (D3). The entrant would have to exclude IP, legal-notice, safety and anything legal-sounding, and avoid giving legal advice.

Platform dependency: Amazon controls the appeal channel (Seller Performance, account health) and can change rules; no Amazon terms about third-party preparers were read. The seller should submit under their own account; the entrant must never take seller credentials.

Some cases (fraud, forged documents, repeated violations per scan-1 SVC-03-E6) are unrecoverable; refund and marketing claims must avoid promising reinstatement, as incumbents do ('No result is guaranteed').
Budget about $500 in the model for a lawyer review of terms and disclaimers; not validated with any bar or attorney.
unverified: Unauthorised-practice-of-law exposure by state (primary sources refused; no search budget left).

The Appeal Guru ($1,495, 50-70% refund guarantee), Amazon Global Appeals (UK package, price and age), amzbase free template content and SupplyKick unrecoverable-case claim: these pages were refused by the fetch tool, so they remain scan-1 agent_reported evidence (E2, E3, E4, E5, E6) and were not re-verified.

Whether a cheap consultant tier ($300-$800) already exists in volume, and its prices; only one web search was possible before the search budget ran out, so the 'at least 3 new alternative queries' work-plan step was not met for this idea.
Success rate on simple categories for a new entrant; ad costs for 'amazon suspended' keywords; Amazon terms on third-party appeal writers.
Review counts and success claims on law-firm pages are self-reported marketing; one page shows blank success table values.
nextStep: Drop it unless a lawyer-reviewed model shows a compliant, credentialed path to the cheap-tier segment; do not spend on it as a stranger with no track record.
